output.body:
# Link token, the token that authorises linking

## In plain words

The token that authorises a [Health Information Provider](/docs/hiecm/v3/getting-started/glossary#hip) to link [care contexts](/docs/hiecm/v3/getting-started/glossary#care-context) to a patient's [ABHA Address](/docs/hiecm/v3/getting-started/glossary#abha-address). It is generated through the link token API and is valid for six months.

## How you know it worked

You can say how long a link token lasts and what to do when it has expired.

## When it goes wrong

A stored link token is used without checking that it is still valid. Validate it before every link. If it has expired, generate a new one through demographic authentication, then link.

# Create a session and get an access token

## In plain words

Every call to [ABDM](/docs/hiecm/v3/getting-started/glossary#abdm) carries an access token, and this call issues it. Send the `clientId` and `clientSecret` issued to you at registration, with `grantType` set to `client_credentials`. It is the one gateway call that needs no bearer token.

The response carries `accessToken`, its lifetime in `expiresIn`, and a `refreshToken`. Read the lifetime from the response rather than assuming one. Create a new session before the token runs out, instead of waiting for a 401.

## Before you start

The client id and client secret for the environment you are calling. Send `REQUEST-ID`, `TIMESTAMP` and `X-CM-ID` on this call too.

## How you know it worked

A 202 whose body carries `accessToken` and `expiresIn`. Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <gateway token>` on every later call.

## When it goes wrong

A 401 with `900901` means the client id or secret is wrong for this environment. A 400 with `ABDM-1015` means the body was refused: check that `grantType` is `client_credentials`.
output.summary: Exchanges your client id and client secret for the access token every ABDM call carries.
output.title: Create a session and get an access token

reply.Text:
No, they are different tokens for different purposes:

**Access token** — Authenticates your application to ABDM. You get it by trading your `clientId` and `clientSecret` at the gateway sessions endpoint, and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every ABDM call. It's short-lived and should be refreshed before it expires.

**Link token** — Authorizes a HIP to link care contexts to a patient's ABHA address during the linking flow. It's issued per-patient through the link token API, valid for six months, and is specific to the patient and your HIP.

In summary: the access token gets you to the API; the link token authorizes you to perform the link operation on a specific patient's records.

See [access token in gateway sessions](https://docs.abdm-integration.in/docs/hiecm/v3/api/gateway/endpoints/gateway-abdm-sessions/01-gateway-post-gateway-v3-sessions#gateway-sessions) and [link token definition](https://docs.abdm-integration.in/docs/hiecm/v3/getting-started/glossary#link-token).
